overall_verdict: Implementable-staged with TWO critical fixes needed before Stage B ships: (1) the ire_dropped set is per-function/flat, not per-CFG-path, so W8-drop on one branch + S4-drop on another branch = leak (not a UAF, but a correctness hole in the design's claim that "W8 and S4 are complementary and non-overlapping"); (2) the design's rc_inc at slot_store fires on EVERY non-owned store INCLUDING re-stores from S3 reassignment loops, creating an unbounded RC inflation in tight loops that never reaches zero (cycle-free permanent leak). Stage A (rc_inc only) can ship after fixing issue #2; Stage B can ship after fixing issue #1. Neither issue is a fundamental design flaw -- both are implementation-level oversights fixable within the design's framework. The core insight (pair every alias with an inc, then dec at scope exit) is sound.

break_scenarios.title: S3 reassignment + S4 scope-exit double-dec on the LAST loop iteration's value
break_scenarios.why_missed: This specific case is actually safe. BUT the design document's Section 8.1 claims 'S3 fires at slot_store time (DURING the function). S4 fires at return time (END of the function). They never fire on the same value at the same point.' This is only accidentally true because S3's rc_drop_reassign drops the OLD value before storing the NEW, and S4 drops the NEW (last) value at return. The design does not prove this invariant for the case where S3 is active on a slot AND S4 is active on the SAME slot -- it just asserts 'No double-free risk' without a formal argument. If a future change makes S3 fire AFTER the store (e.g., for deferred cleanup), the invariant breaks silently. The design should explicitly state: 'S3 drops value V_old at store of V_new; S4 drops V_last at return; V_old != V_last by construction because every S3-eligible slot is stored at least twice (otherwise S3 never fires).'

break_scenarios.title: rc_inc on EVERY slot_store of a non-owned value in a tight loop inflates RC without bound when the same value is re-stored
break_scenarios.why_missed: The design's Section 3.1 says rc_inc fires at slot_store for borrowed values. Section 8.1 says S3 reassignment-drop handles overwrite. But S3 ONLY fires for slots where EVERY store is ire_owned (fresh make_list/dict/struct/closure). A slot that receives borrowed values (index_get results) is NOT in S3's drop set. So the rc_inc at each store is emitted, but the rc_dec on overwrite is NOT. The design ASSUMES S3 and S4 together cover all cases, but S3's prerequisite (all stores are owned-producer) is incompatible with S4's new rc_inc-on-borrowed-store. The gap: a slot repeatedly stored with borrowed values gets rc_inc on each store but rc_dec only ONCE at scope exit. The design needs an EXPANDED S3 that drops the old value on EVERY overwrite (not just owned-producer slots) now that rc_inc ensures the invariant holds.

break_scenarios.title: ire_dropped is per-function, not per-CFG-path: W8 drop on one branch leaks on another
break_scenarios.why_missed: The design's Section 8.3 says 'S4's scope-exit emission must check ire_dropped and skip any slot already dropped by W8.' But ire_dropped is a flat per-function dict, not a per-basic-block or per-path set. When blocks are emitted sequentially (for block in blocks), W8 adds to ire_dropped in one block's emission, and a later block's return terminator sees it. If the two blocks are on DIFFERENT control-flow paths (if/else branches), the drop in one path poisons the other path's scope-exit logic. The design needs either: (a) per-return-point dropped sets (clone ire_dropped before each block emission), or (b) restrict W8 to dominator blocks only (a block that dominates the return), or (c) emit S4 drops at EVERY return independently of W8's flat set (accepting potential double-dec on the W8 path, mitigated by checking RC > 0 before freeing).

break_scenarios.title: Closure capturing a local that is then scope-exit-dropped: rc_inc at capture vs rc_dec at return is a RACE with the closure's lifetime
break_scenarios.why_missed: While this specific scenario is safe, the design does NOT specify drop ORDER at scope exit. Section 4.4 says 'for slot_name in keys(e.ire_scope_drop)' -- dict key iteration order in NOVA is insertion order (hash map). If a container (data) is dropped BEFORE a slot holding one of its elements (a), the recursive dec inside nova_rc_free decrements the element; then the slot's dec decrements it again. With the rc_inc design, the counts are correct (3 refs total, 3 decs total). But if a CYCLE exists (container A holds element that points back to A via a closure capture), the recursive free can re-enter on a partially-freed object. NOVA does not have true cycles (no mutable self-references in the value model), but closures capturing their own containing list (e.g., a list of callbacks where each callback captures the list) can create one. The design does not address cycle detection or mention that nova_rc_free is not re-entrant-safe for cycles.

break_scenarios.title: for_iter_init list case: iterator register aliases source list, design's proposed borrow-marking is unsound when source is unknown type
break_scenarios.why_missed: The design acknowledges this in Section 3.7 and Open Question #2 but proposes a heuristic: 'check ire_reg_types[args[0]] -- if list, mark borrow; if dict or unknown, mark owned.' The 'unknown' -> 'owned' fallback is UNSOUND because for_iter_init on a list returns the list handle UNMODIFIED (no allocation, no rc_inc). Marking it owned and then scope-exit-dropping it decrements a value the function does not own. The only sound options are: (a) ALWAYS mark the for_iter_init result as borrowed (leaks the dict-keys case), (b) have for_iter_init rc_inc the list case in the RUNTIME (adds ~15ns per for-in loop but closes the hole), or (c) never scope-exit-drop for_iter_init results (special-case them out of S4). Option (b) is the clean fix.

break_scenarios.title: nova_rc_inc calls nova_rc_is_managed which calls nova_mem_find_tag on every slot_store: ~25ns per store is catastrophic in the self-hosting compiler
break_scenarios.why_missed: Section 10.1 says 'For a typical function with 5 local slots, that's ~75-125ns per function call.' This ONLY counts the function-entry stores, ignoring re-stores inside loops and conditionals. The real count is: (number of slot_store IR instructions executed at runtime) * 25ns, which for a compiler processing a large program is in the millions. The design does mention a Phase 2 typed fast-path optimization but does not acknowledge the Phase 1 regression on the compiler itself. Since the compiler is the GATE for every other program, a 10% compile-time regression violates the 'compilation speed is a feature' principle. The fix (Phase 2 typed elision for int/float/bool slots, and a nova_rc_inc_fast for known-heap) needs to be Phase 1, not Phase 2.

break_scenarios.title: W8 uses list_free_local/dict_free_local (no element RC) but S4 uses nova_rc_dec (with element RC): mixing them on different paths creates RC count mismatch
break_scenarios.why_missed: The design explicitly acknowledges in Section 8.3 that 'W8 currently uses list_free_local/dict_free_local (unsound for shared elements). When S4 is active, W8 should also switch to nova_rc_dec for correctness. This is a Phase 2 concern.' But the design ALSO says in Phase 1, W5b still fires as a fallback for slots not in ire_scope_drop. The mixing of three different drop strategies (W8=list_free_local, W5b=list_free_local, S4=nova_rc_dec) on the same function's slots, depending on control flow path, creates an inconsistent RC state. A slot dropped by W8 (no child dec) on one path and by S4 (with child dec) on another path has different child RC counts. The design does not specify how to reconcile this. The safe answer is: when NOVA_T8_SCOPE is active, W8 MUST use nova_rc_dec too (not deferred to Phase 2).

break_scenarios.title: Returned value exclusion uses ire_load_origin which is a flat map: returning a value computed from a chain of operations loses the source slot
break_scenarios.why_missed: The design's Section 4.4 uses ire_load_origin to find the returned slot: 'if contains(ire_load_origin, ret_reg): returned_slot = ire_load_origin[ret_reg]'. But ire_load_origin is only set for registers produced by slot_load. If the compiler emits a return that directly uses a call result register (without going through slot_store + slot_load), ire_load_origin is empty for that register, returned_slot is '', and the slot exclusion fails. The design acknowledges ire_load_origin is set at slot_load (Section 3.1 mentions it) but does not verify that EVERY return path goes through slot_load. In practice, NOVA's IR likely always does slot_store then slot_load before return (since all values go through alloca slots), but this is an implicit assumption not verified in the design. If the IR optimizer ever eliminates a redundant load (e.g., forwarding the store directly to the return), the assumption breaks.

break_scenarios.title: rc_inc at make_struct for non-owned fields double-counts when field was already rc_inc'd at slot_store
break_scenarios.why_missed: This is actually correct by the design's own logic -- every alias-creating site (slot_store AND make_struct field pack) gets its own rc_inc, and each has a matching rc_dec (scope-exit for the slot, recursive free for the struct). The counts balance. However, the design does not call out that the SAME value may receive MULTIPLE rc_incs (one per aliasing event) and that this is intentional. A reader (or implementer) might optimize away the 'redundant' inc at make_struct because 'the slot already inc'd it.' That would be a soundness bug. The design should add an explicit note: 'A value may receive multiple rc_incs if it is aliased into multiple locations. Each inc has a matching dec. Do not deduplicate.'

break_scenarios.title: M:N scheduler fiber migration: a green task's scope-exit drops fire on carrier thread A, but the task's locals may have been allocated on carrier thread B's heap region
break_scenarios.why_missed: The design's Section 8.4 discusses arena mode interaction but does not discuss the M:N scheduler at all. The memory memo (project_mn_scheduler_step1.md) notes that green tasks are fiber-migrated between carriers. If the runtime ever moves to per-carrier memory pools (a natural optimization for M:N schedulers, used by Go and Erlang), nova_rc_is_managed's pointer validation would break for migrated tasks. The design should include an explicit assumption: 'All carriers share a single global heap. nova_rc_is_managed's validation (nova_heap_base, IsBadReadPtr) is carrier-agnostic. If per-carrier heaps are added in the future, the validation must be updated to check all carrier heaps.'

break_scenarios.title: Channel send deep-copies but rc_inc at slot_store still fires on the source side, inflating RC of a value that will never be dec'd on the sender side
break_scenarios.why_missed: This scenario is safe. Including it to confirm: channel_send's deep_copy creates an independent object, so the sender-side RC accounting is unaffected. The design correctly identifies this in Section 3.8 (channel_send -> deep_copy -> fresh). No issue.

break_scenarios.title: nova_rc_inc is not atomic in the bootstrap runtime (nova-compiler/nova_runtime.c) -- bootstrap compiler is single-threaded so this is fine, but the DESIGN DOCUMENT references the output runtime's atomic path without noting the bootstrap discrepancy
break_scenarios.why_missed: The design document does not distinguish between the two runtime files. It references 'nova_runtime.c line 7961' for nova_rc_inc and 'nova_runtime.c line 8013' for nova_rc_dec, which are the output runtime's line numbers. The bootstrap runtime at nova-compiler/nova_runtime.c has DIFFERENT implementations (no arena bit check, no oddball check, no atomic path, no NOVA_MEM_STRUCT in rc_free). If Stage A/B are tested against the bootstrap runtime instead of the output runtime, the test results are invalid. The design should specify: 'All testing uses output/nova_runtime.c. The bootstrap runtime is NOT updated for S4 (it lacks NOVA_MEM_STRUCT handling in rc_free, so struct field RC is broken there).'
